what: Ben's Fusion check F2: Combine Join of two 20 × 20 × 10 boxes 10 mm apart. No error, no warning; the target stays Body 1 and the tool's box becomes a new body, Body 3 (Fusion's own words and numbers). Both boxes stand on the XY plane, so their bottoms and tops lie in one plane but 10 mm apart: no face pair is near, so nothing here waits for 36a (35b refuses only faces that overlap on one plane); if 35 refuses this, that refusal is the bug.

recipe.do: Start a new part and delete its ready-made box (feature-1) from the timeline, as the L bracket's make does, so the counter goes on from 2.
Create Sketch on the top plane XY.
Rectangle tool: click (0, 0), then (20, 20) (points 3, 4, 6, 8; lines 5, 7, 9, 10). The first click lands on the origin, which is not a pin.
Create Sketch on the top plane XY.
Rectangle tool: click (30, 0), then (50, 20) (points and lines 13 to 20; Body 1 seen along Z offers (0 or 20, 0 or 20) and (10, 0), (20, 10), (10, 20), (0, 10), none here).
Extrude the sketch 10 (z 0 to 10): Body 2, 10 mm to the right of Body 1.
Combine: target Body 1, tool Body 2, Join, Keep tools off. The two share no point, so the result is one body per piece (decision 3).

volume.why: the target, unchanged: 20 × 20 × 10 = 4000, keeping body:feature-11 (34a rule 1: the target's piece keeps its id)

tolerance.why: LINEAR (10 nm): every crossing here is between planes at round numbers, exact, so no intersection measures past LINEAR and nothing may grow (B0 decision 5)
